source: Derived from the public OpenINTEL data dictionary (https://openintel.nl/background/dictionary/), reduced to a DNSSEC-relevant analysis view.
notes: This is an ANALYSIS dictionary, not a verbatim copy of the OpenINTEL Parquet schema.
Each field lists 'openintel_native_fields': the real OpenINTEL column names this analysis field is derived from.
'available_from' is the earliest date on which the field is considered reliably populated in the measurement corpus.
Indicators referencing fields absent from this dictionary are classified non_queryable by the schema checker.

'openintel_native_fields' must list only columns that are genuine alternative sources of the same value: the reader COALESCEs them. The Hive partition columns year/month/day are deliberately NOT listed under 'timestamp' -- they are components of the partition path, not fallbacks for a measurement time, and on real S3 data DuckDB types year as BIGINT while month and day are VARCHAR, so coalescing them is both meaningless and a hard bind error.
'measurement_id' has no column in the real OpenINTEL corpus. It resolves in the synthetic sample only, and reads as null against real data.

0.2.0 adds the NSEC3 parameter, DNSKEY format, RSA key size and TLSA columns needed to evidence RFC 9276, RFC 4034, RFC 5155 opt-out and the DANE RFCs. Every added field maps to a column verified present in the 93-column OpenINTEL forward-DNS schema.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: Measurement timestamp (UTC) at which the DNS response was observed.

fields.name: domain
fields.description: Fully qualified domain name that was queried.

fields.name: zone
fields.description: Zone or TLD the measurement partition belongs to.

fields.name: rr_type
fields.description: DNS resource record type of the observed response record (DNSKEY, DS, RRSIG, NSEC, NSEC3, NSEC3PARAM, CDS, CDNSKEY, ...).

fields.name: algorithm
fields.description: DNSSEC algorithm number carried by the record (IANA DNSSEC Algorithm Numbers). Algorithm 0 in CDS/CDNSKEY is the RFC 8078 delete signal.

fields.name: digest_type
fields.description: DS/CDS digest type (1 = SHA-1, 2 = SHA-256, 4 = SHA-384).

fields.name: key_tag
fields.description: DNSSEC key tag identifying the key a DS/RRSIG/CDS record refers to.

fields.name: flags
fields.description: DNSKEY/NSEC3 flags field, rendered as a string. Only reliably exported in later measurement generations.

fields.name: source
fields.description: OpenINTEL measurement source / partition identifier (e.g. the zone file or top list the name was drawn from).

fields.name: measurement_id
fields.description: Opaque identifier of the individual measurement run or object the row came from.

fields.name: nsec3_iterations
fields.description: NSEC3 iteration count (RFC 5155 s3.2, a 16-bit field, 0-65535). Every extra iteration is another SHA-1 pass a validating resolver must perform on a negative answer, which is the root cause of CVE-2023-50868. RFC 9276 recommends 0.

fields.name: nsec3_salt
fields.description: NSEC3 salt as published. RFC 9276 recommends an empty salt: it adds no security against a modern attacker and costs a zone re-salt to change.

fields.name: nsec3_flags
fields.description: NSEC3 flags as an integer. Bit 0 is Opt-Out (RFC 5155 s6): when set, unsigned delegations may be skipped in the hash chain. Distinct from the generic `flags` field, which is a string coalesced across DNSKEY/CDNSKEY/NSEC3 and cannot be compared numerically.

fields.name: dnskey_protocol
fields.description: DNSKEY/CDNSKEY protocol octet. RFC 4034 s2.1.2 fixes it at 3, so this evidences the RFC 4034 record format specifically rather than DNSSEC in general.

fields.name: rsa_key_bitsize
fields.description: Modulus size of an RSA DNSKEY/CDNSKEY in bits. Carries the operational key-strength signal RFC 6781 discusses; null for every non-RSA algorithm, which is itself informative.

fields.name: rrsig_type_covered
fields.description: RR type an RRSIG covers (RFC 4034 s3.1.1). Present only on RRSIG records, so it evidences the RFC 4034 signature record format directly.

fields.name: tlsa_usage
fields.description: TLSA certificate usage (RFC 6698 s2.1.1): 0 PKIX-TA, 1 PKIX-EE, 2 DANE-TA, 3 DANE-EE. RFC 7671 gives operational guidance that favours 2 and 3.

fields.name: tlsa_selector
fields.description: TLSA selector (RFC 6698 s2.1.2): 0 full certificate, 1 SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

fields.name: tlsa_matchtype
fields.description: TLSA matching type (RFC 6698 s2.1.3): 0 exact, 1 SHA-256, 2 SHA-512.
